title: Can ChatGPT analyze your portfolio? Astor vs. ChatGPT for investing
summary: Yes, in the US ChatGPT can now read your holdings. Here’s how it compares with Astor, a personal investing agent and SEC-registered adviser.
body_markdown:
## Why Astor is the better fit for your investments


In our view, judged on the criteria in the table, a tool built for one job, helping with the investments you already own, does that job better than a general assistant you have to configure.


Astor knows your actual holdings across brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts, through connections to most major US institutions, including Robinhood, Schwab and Coinbase. It watches them without being asked. When something matters, it texts you what happened, why it matters to you and what you could do, and you can reply in the same thread with a follow-up, the way you’d text a person. Every alert links to the reasoning and sources behind it, which matters because the AI can be wrong. You can read more about[talking to Astor in iMessage](https://www.astor.app/blog/talk-to-astor-in-imessage) .


Astor is also a registered investment adviser that owes clients a fiduciary duty, which by OpenAI’s own description ChatGPT isn’t. It never trades or moves money in your connected accounts, and it never charges a percentage of your assets. If you want to act on an idea,[Text to Trade](https://www.astor.app/blog/introducing-text-to-trade) , available on Max plans, lets you describe it in a sentence, review a proposed basket sized against what you already own, and approve each trade before it executes in your own Robinhood agentic account. You make every decision.


You don’t have to choose only one. Using ChatGPT to learn and Astor to watch what you own is a reasonable setup. You can[see how Astor works](https://www.astor.app/#how-it-works) or read[what a personal investing agent is](https://www.astor.app/blog/what-is-a-personal-investing-agent) .
